Title: Diagnosis
Details: The corresponding issue report describes that tooltip text in the UI is displayed with HTML entities such as " instead of the intended characters. This strongly suggests a missing escaping or decoding step in tooltip generation. Inspecting the implementation of StandardToolTipTagFragmentGenerator.generateToolTipFragment reveals that it directly returns the toolTipText without applying any escaping. Recent issue reports mention similar encoding or escaping problems in related UI components, reinforcing the suspicion that this method lacks proper handling. The behavior observed in the code matches the issue report's symptoms, indicating that missing escaping in this method is the likely root cause.

After providing this diagnosis, you will be prompted to suggest which methods would be the best locations to be fixed. The answers should be in the form of `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` without commentary (one per line), as your answer will be automatically processed before finally being presented to the user.

messages.content: "182 :     public int compareTo(Object other) {\n183 :         return iValue - ((ValuedEnum) other).iValue;\n184 :     }"

Title: Diagnosis
Details: The failing test case `testCompareTo_otherEnumType()` attempts to compare two different enum types, `ValuedColorEnum.BLUE` and `ValuedLanguageEnum.ENGLISH`, which are presumably subclasses of `ValuedEnum`. The test expects a `ClassCastException` when comparing different enum types using `compareTo`.

The bug report states that `ValuedEnum.compareTo(Object other)` is not type-safe and can return `0` if the int values (`iValue`) of two different subclasses are the same, which is incorrect behavior since they are conceptually different types.

Examining the `compareTo` method in `ValuedEnum`:
```
public int compareTo(Object other) {
    return iValue - ((ValuedEnum) other).iValue;
}
```
This method simply casts `other` to `ValuedEnum` without any type checking or verification that `other` is the same subclass as `this`. This can lead to the method comparing `iValue`s of different enum types silently without throwing any exception, violating type safety.

The test expects a `ClassCastException` because comparing different enum types should not be allowed, but the current implementation merely casts the parameter to the base class and compares `iValue`s, so no exception is thrown. This explains why the test fails.

Hence, the root cause of the bug is the lack of type safety in `ValuedEnum.compareTo`, which blindly casts to the base class without verifying that `other` is an instance of the same subclass.

This confirms the bug report's observation and explains the failure seen in the test `testCompareTo_otherEnumType`.

Next, I can suggest the best location(s) for fixes.
org.apache.commons.lang.enums.ValuedEnum.compareTo(java.lang.Object)
